evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a game is a foundational capability and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators ... access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators to access a game inherently depends on a game existing to invite them to.

evaluations.evidence: start a round ... so that we can estimate it
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes an existing game/session context in which the round occurs.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing all items in a session depends on items being created/added to that session first.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item inherently depends on there being a list of items already available.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item to a list presupposes a game/session context in which that list exists.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item inherently depends on items having been created/added first.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item inherently depends on items existing in the list first.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates depends on an estimation round where estimates can be given and collected.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average inherently depends on estimates having been provided for an item/round.

evaluations.evidence: filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling based on all estimators' cards depends on the existence of estimator participation and card/estimate submission.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate depends on an estimation context (item/round) where an estimate is being agreed upon.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating inherently depends on having previously estimated the story in the same session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories can be implemented as a standalone capability; it does not inherently require another specific story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste entry is a standalone input mechanism and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games depends on games having been created/stored previously.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript depends on a game having occurred and been stored as a previous game.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript inherently depends on the ability to view/access a stored transcript.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript inherently depends on the ability to view/access a stored transcript.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game inherently depends on games existing to be deleted.

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is self-contained and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently depends on accounts existing (being created) to authenticate against.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details inherently depends on an existing account (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account inherently depends on an account existing (and typically being able to access it).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a cross-cutting presentation requirement and does not inherently depend on a specific other story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders inherently depend on accounts existing with stored email addresses/credentials.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Selecting a card scale inherently depends on having an estimation/game flow where cards are used.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators (with a limit) depends on the base invitation capability and an existing game to invite them to.

evaluations.evidence: join a game ... page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining a game via a received URL inherently depends on the game existing and the invitation/URL mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item being estimated depends on an item being selected/active for the round.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items in the session depends on items having been added/available in the session.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: This depends on estimators being able to join and submit estimates in a round.

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates ... after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates after everyone has estimated depends on the ability for estimators to join and provide estimates.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until ... all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the existence of estimate submission and the reveal/completion mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Prior estimates can only exist if estimates have been recorded in earlier rounds for the same story.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: This depends on a current round existing and estimates being given/recorded.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer for participants inherently depends on a multiplayer game/session context with participants present.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Resetting the timer based on everyone playing an estimate depends on the timer existing and the estimate-play/reveal flow.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds depends on rounds having occurred and their stories/estimates being recorded.

evaluations.evidence: cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card ordering across draws depends on the existence of draws/estimation rounds using cards.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing an estimate depends on the draw/estimate submission lifecycle being implemented.

evaluations.evidence: thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a participant photo near played cards depends on having the card-play UI and participant identity in the game.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: A glossary can be created independently of other functional stories.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Database indexing is an internal optimization task that can be performed without requiring a particular other story to be implemented first (beyond having a database schema, which is not specified as another story).

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser support is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a self-contained quality requirement and does not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Predictable URLs are a self-contained design/quality requirement and do not inherently depend on another specific story.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages can be implemented independently as a cross-cutting UI requirement without requiring another specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Storing results (anonymized or not) inherently depends on results/estimates being generated and stored by the game.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Usage metrics inherently depend on the game being used and usage data being captured from core gameplay.
